subject: Sample size CFA in R based on pilot study

messages.author: b5314d88ca467034
messages.subject: Sample size CFA in R based on pilot study
parts:
Hi,
I am developing a new scale and want to test the fit indices of the factor structure in a CFA. I already ran one pilot study and want to have the sample size for a power of .80 for the next study using CFA. Especially since in my pilot study the RMSEA was over .08.
I saw lavaan and simsem can be useful but I have no idea how to use them with a pilot study. 
Any tips?

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: Sample size CFA in R based on pilot study
parts:
Hi,

My colleagues and I are investigating how to solve this issue with simsem and we still haven`t published any results, but here is a sample of what we are doing
```
#Population model
Population<-'#specific factors
F1=~0.80*I1+0.74*I2+0.68*I3
F2=~0.62*I4+0.56*I5+0.5*I6

#thresholds
I1|1.028*t1
I2|0.539*t1
I3|0.156*t1
I4|(-0.179)*t1
I5|(-0.565)*t1
I6|(-1.067)*t1

#latent mean
F1~0*1; F2~0*1

#latent variance
F1~~1*F1; F2~~1*F2

#Factor correlation
F1~~0.5*F2'

#Tested Model
unidimensional<-'#structure
F1=~I1+I2+I3+I4+I5+I6'

# Run the simulation
sim.n490<-simsem::sim(nRep = 1e4, model = unidimensional, n = 490,
                      generate = Population, lavaanfun = "cfa", seed = 123,
                      multicore = TRUE, estimator = "WLSMV",std.lv = TRUE,
                      ordered = TRUE)

#get main results, such as power for each parameter
print(simsem::summary(sim.n490))

# Get omnibus power
print(simsem::getPowerFit(sim.n490, alpha = .05, cutoff = c(RMSEA.SCALED=0.08), usedFit = "RMSEA.SCALED")
```

The full procedure would be too long to describe here, so I will type some of the main considerations to take care of:
  • The factor loadings you have to place in the population model are unstandardized loadings, but by setting the latent mean to zero and the latent standard deviation to one, the unstandardized loadings are equal to the standardized loadings when the model is right.
  • If you try to fit the correct model or a model with more latent variables than necessary, you almost always validate the model despite the sample size. Thus, your focus should be what `n` discriminates your model from simpler models. In this example, I wish to validate a 2-first order factor model, so I have to discard the possibility that the model is unidimensional (I know that, in this example, it is 490 for a power of .90 using RMSEA.CI.LOWER.SCALED < .05  as cutoff). If your model is more complex (3 factors, second order, bifactor), than I suggest to always begin estimating the `n` that discriminates the simplest model (unidimensional), and after finding it, find for the intermediary models.
  • You can order simsem to change the sample size in each simulation by setting `nRep=NULL` and `n` as a vector (e.g.: `n = c(400,450,500)`), but it does only one simulation for each `n`, what can be very unstable when sample size is small. "Small" is relative for the complexity of the models (population and tested), kind of item (intervalar or ordinal), and estimator. So sometimes, `n = 150` is a big sample and other times `n = 2000` is small. So, unfortunately, I recommend setting `nRep` for a big number (e.g.: 1e4) and change `n` to believable numbers until you find the most appropriate number.
  • Sometimes, `lavaan` gives an error that makes `simsem` returns no result. I've talked to Dr. Rosseel, who is trying to fix it, but so far, there is no definitive solution. You can try to reduce the `nRep` and/or increase `n` to try to solve it, but sometimes there seems to be no hope. Since this seems to be related to how `lavaan` computes robust SEs, I suppose it is acceptable to change the estimator for one that does not compute robust SEs, even if this reduces your power.
Best,

Yago

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Sample size CFA in R based on pilot study
parts:
Yago wrote:
>>>
You can order simsem to change the sample size in each simulation by setting `nRep=NULL` and `n` as a vector (e.g.: `n = c(400,450,500)`), but it does only one simulation for each `n`, what can be very unstable when sample size is small.
>>>

For what it is worth...
n = 200:1000 is probably more useful for simulations that do not use a factorial design but rather seek to estimate the shape of the function of a dependent variable conditional on n (e.g., a regression line). Such a design incorporates sampling error as single case residuals instead of group standard deviations.

n = rep(seq(from=200, to=500, by=100), each=1000) can be used for a factorial design with, in this case 1000 replications for each of four conditions.

If the error returned by lavaan stops the simulation, one option might be to provide a custom function to simsem that is just a wrapper around the lavaan model fitting function (e.g., lavaan(), sem()) that encloses it in a try() function and takes the desired action in case of an error.  This will slow down the simulation but may offer a feasible work around for models that converge rapidly.  (I have not actually implemented this and could be missing something, but is seems prima facie workable.)

Keith
